subject: Connection gateway ACLs, DNS & mTLS — integration checklist
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@hyperflux.ai>, infra-team@hyperflux.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + immediate networking asks

Hi Sam / HyperFlux infra team —

Great to meet you all on the demo earlier. Recap and concrete asks below so we all have the same scope moving into the tech deep-dive: 

1) Integration scope summary (what they plan to use):
- SDK-based request routing for synchronous chat + structured tool-calling outputs
- Embeddings for semantic search; reranker on top of candidate set
- Preference to run traffic over private connectivity (VPC endpoint) to avoid public egress

2) Immediate networking items we need to validate today:
- Will you provide a VPC endpoint (privatelink) or do you want Redwood to peer into your VPC?
- IP allowlist for egress outbound to Redwood control plane (we provided the list on call; attaching reference doc)
- DNS: Do you have strict egress DNS resolution policies (we need to ensure our endpoint hostnames resolve appropriately over peering/private link)?
- mTLS: HyperFlux asked about mutual TLS for inter-service auth — please confirm whether you can terminate mTLS at the gateway or require mTLS end-to-end to app instances.

3) Auth & SDK notes for follow-up:
- We support short-lived service tokens via your KMS; we can also integrate with your Okta OIDC for service principal issuance (if you prefer).
- SDK will include structured-output schema (JSON schema) and a reranker hook for embeddings — we’ll need a sample corpus (~500 docs) to validate scoring latency.

Next steps I propose: scoring deep-dive with Ben (runtime/latency), network session with Priyom (VPC/egress/DNS/mTLS), and a shared checklist for the procurement/security folks.

I attached our private connectivity guide and the network requirements spreadsheet referenced on the call. Can you confirm who from your side will own the VPC/edge work?

Thanks—
Avery

Thanks Avery — good summary. Quick answers from infra: 

- Ownership: we'll own the VPC endpoint. My infra lead (looped at infra-team@hyperflux.ai) will manage peering and route tables.
- IP allowlist: we'll provision the outbound allowlist for Redwood control plane; our security requires a CIDR-range + port list — your guide is helpful.
- DNS: we run split-horizon DNS; the VPC endpoint will resolve internally. We may need to create a private hosted zone pointing to your endpoint IPs.
- mTLS: we prefer mTLS terminated at the HyperFlux ingress gateway; however, we can support mutual mTLS all the way to the instance if Redwood requires it for authentication. We need details on cert exchange and rotation cadence.

Action: infra-team will start filling the spreadsheet tonight. Can Ben follow up on expected port numbers, timeouts, and TLS ciphers? Priyom — can you coordinate for the routing and private DNS mapping?

Sam
CTO (interim), HyperFlux
sam.park@hyperflux.ai

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + immediate networking asks

Appreciate the quick turn Sam — a few technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side: 

- Ports & protocols: primary egress is HTTPS (443) + gRPC (443) for streaming. We may also ask for occasional healthcheck endpoints on 8080 (ingress to Redwood side). We will include explicit port/host header examples in the refreshed spreadsheet.

- Keepalive / timeouts: recommended idle keepalive of 60s for streaming connections, request timeout of 120s for longer generation runs (configurable per-route).

- Private DNS: if you create a private hosted zone that resolves our endpoint names to the VPC endpoint IPs, the SDK will transparently route over the private path. We'll provide the endpoint hostnames (redwood-<region>.svc.internal.redwood) once the peering is live.

- mTLS details: Redwood can operate in two modes: 
  1) TLS-only with bearer tokens (simpler; we rotate tokens via your KMS)
  2) mTLS + token (mutual cert authentication plus tokens) — supports stricter identity guarantees.

For cert exchange: we can accept a short-lived leaf cert signed by your private CA (SCEP/ACME-style rotation is supported) or we can provision a cert from our managed CA and share chain details. Rotation cadence we recommend is 7-14 days for short-lived leaf certs.

- Embeddings/reranker: to validate latency of reranking, we need a 500-row CSV (id, text, metadata) and a sample query set (~50 queries). We’ll run a small benchmark in your dev VPC and share results. Estimated warm latency for embedding + rerank ~ 40-120ms per query depending on vector size and reranker complexity.

I'll attach a short checklist and draft the port list into the spreadsheet. Priyom — can you propose two 45-minute slots tomorrow for a routing/mTLS session?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
